| step | problem | handling-time world |

It is a pure chain, so no write is computed early and no two orders exist. Base

**No real-world waits.** Every input is an authoritative record already in `initial_state` (the account, its

**Tools do not judge the prerequisites.** `lodge_contract_gallon_booking_8fcb503b`,
`update_contract_price_of_record_9db7726a`, `settle_undrawn_contract_gallons_1dbcf678` and

**Consequences of the charter-global defects, demonstrated on this task's world and scored solution:**

- **F5 (_difficulty.md § findings) — the decisive one.** Base `energy_lifecycle_progression`: "A member
  closes an account of their own accord with **nothing owing** …", with
  `params.closure_requires: [zero_balance, zero_undrawn_contract_gallons, no_budget_plan_in_mid_year]`.
  `energy_ext_closure_settlement` declares `overwrite: []`, yet its scored quantity is a **positive**
  closing balance (this auditor's derivation: 3307.31) which the `owner="user"` tool
  `close_energy_account_7515982f` writes onto the account as `account_balance`. On this task's world the
  balance is not nil at any point before the close: `amount_standing_d` = 3368.40 at step 4, and
  `user_scenario` has the member paying **after** the call ("she will put a cheque in the post for it this
  week"), so no payment write can precede the close. Two defensible answers: under the inherited base
  sentence the only correct act is to quote the figure and decline to close until it is paid (terminal
  state: the account stays `active`); under the extended policy the account is closed now carrying
  3307.31. The terminal state itself differs, not merely a number.
- **F4** — base `energy_contract_gallons_program`: "A member who wants out of a booking before the gallons
  are drawn pays the programme's cancellation charge per gallon cancelled." The Bulk Farm Fuel Delivery
  Account's `contract_cancellation_fee_per_gallon_usd` is 0.1000. Reading the base sentence, the undrawn
  settlement is **14319.20**; under the extended `cancellation_charge_relief` ladder (0.0600) it is
  **14506.40**, and the closing balance moves with it. Two defensible answers.
- **O5** — the account is a Bulk Farm Fuel Delivery Account, whose `price_basis` is
  `rack_plus_margin_on_the_delivery_day`, so the "contracted price of record" this task writes at step 2
  never prices a gallon on that programme; it matters only through step 3's settlement price. Observation.
- **F1, F2, F3, F6** — bear on task 0, not on this task's scope.

**SOURCE-TASK RED (T1) — the price the booked gallons are credited at is not fixed by any policy.**
`lodge_contract_gallon_booking_8fcb503b` takes `price_per_gallon` ("the fixed price the booked gallons draw
at") and writes `amount = booked_gallons × price_per_gallon` onto the account.
`energy_ext_prebuy_booking_credit` `computes: booked_gallons` only; its `rule` never mentions a price. No
other policy in force supplies one either: base `energy_contract_gallons_program` says only that "the money
is taken at the booking"; base `energy_pricing` gives this programme
`price_basis: rack_plus_margin_on_the_delivery_day`, and no rack figure exists anywhere in `initial_state`
or in any finder; `energy_orders.b3d73765-…` carries `requested_gallons` but no price; and the persona
supplies none ("without asking what it will cost her"). Yet the figure is load-bearing:
`energy_ext_closure_settlement.compute.commitment_d` sums the booking line's `amount`, so the scored closing
balance moves with it. Recomputed over the defensible candidate readings:

| reading of `price_per_gallon` | source a solver could cite | price of record (step 2) | undrawn settlement (step 3) | closing balance (step 4) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3.0900 | "the price billed on the most recent stop the member called in" (ticket `ET-6712611`, 2026-10-28) | 3.09 | 14506.40 | **3307.31** |
| 3.1400 | the most recent will-call price before the after-hours stop (`ET-6712318`, 2026-09-20) | 3.09 | 14506.40 | **3567.31** |
| 3.1200 | the price of the day the signed request was taken, 2025-11-20 (nearest stop `ET-6710221`, 2025-12-08) | 3.09 | 14506.40 | **3463.31** |
| 2.9800 | the first stop of the twelve months (`ET-6709884`, 2025-10-15) | 3.07 | 14459.60 | **2782.11** |

Four defensible answers for the scored closing balance. Recorded as `SOURCE-TASK RED`; the rest of this
file is derived on the 3.0900 reading, which is the one the charter's own phrase "the price billed on the
most recent stop the member called in" (used verbatim by both
`energy_ext_contract_price_of_record` and `energy_ext_undrawn_gallons_disposition`) most nearly supports.

### problem_chain

**Root problem.** `user_scenario`: "the bulk farm diesel account is finished with … she wants the account
closed off properly and told what she owes to be done with it. She would like that settled on this call."
The only policy whose `computes` is what an energy account closes at is `energy_ext_closure_settlement`
(`computes: closing_balance_usd`, `target_tool: close_energy_account_7515982f`, `owner="user"`).

**Walking the prerequisite sentences down from the root.**

*Edge 1 — the root's own sentence.* "The balance the account closes at is fixed only after the account
carries, for every booking whose gallons stand undrawn, the money applied against it when those gallons are
released." Judged against the raw DB at frozen_time: `energy_accounts.9762da2a-…` carries
`contract_gallons: 0` and `contract_price_per_gallon: 0.0`, and `energy_deliveries` holds **no**
`energy_contract_gallons_booked` row at all. There is therefore no booking whose gallons stand undrawn, and
the state the sentence waits on **holds vacuously at the opening**. See `SOURCE-CHAIN RED (C1)` below.

*Edge 2 — `energy_ext_undrawn_gallons_disposition`'s sentence.* "The money applied against a booking on the
gallons standing undrawn is worked out only after the account's contracted price of record stands at a
price worked out from the bookings the account carries." At frozen_time
`contract_price_per_gallon` is `0.0` — the nil price the edge's `condition` names. **Unmet.** Resolved by
`update_contract_price_of_record_9db7726a`.

*Edge 3 — `energy_ext_contract_price_of_record`'s sentence.* "The contracted price of record is written only
after the gallons standing to the member's credit take in every signed pre-buy request registered with the
energy desk." `energy_orders.b3d73765-…` is a registered, signed `contract_gallons_booking` for 7 000
gallons (2025-11-20) and no booked gallons stand to the member's credit. **Unmet.** Resolved by
`lodge_contract_gallon_booking_8fcb503b`.

`energy_ext_prebuy_booking_credit` carries no prerequisite, so the walk terminates.

**Derived tree** (identical in shape to the `prerequisite` declarations):

```
energy_ext_closure_settlement                       (root; owner=user write)
└── value_input → energy_ext_undrawn_gallons_disposition   (owner=agent write)
    └── value_input → energy_ext_contract_price_of_record  (owner=agent write)
        └── value_input → energy_ext_prebuy_booking_credit (owner=user write)
```
n = 3 prerequisite problems; floor max(n−1,1) = 2 `value_input` edges; **3** present. No cycle, and no edge
crosses into task 0's component.

**Per-edge load-bearing run** (recomputed on this task's world, everything else unchanged):

| run | closing balance |
| --- | --- |
| whole chain (gold path, price 3.0900) | **3307.31** |
| skip the undrawn settlement (step 3) | 17813.71 |
| skip the price-of-record rewrite (step 2) — settlement price falls to min(0.0, 3.09) = 0.0, the undrawn settlement to 0.00 | 19393.71 |
| skip the booking (step 1) — no booking exists, so nothing downstream fires | 1745.71 |

Every edge bears weight.

**No parallel edges**, so no terminal-state ambiguity from ordering.

**No waiting.** Steps 1–4 are all performable on the call; nothing needs a real-world event.

**Customer's own writes.** Two problems of the tree are `owner="user"` —
`lodge_contract_gallon_booking_8fcb503b` (step 1) and `close_energy_account_7515982f` (step 4) — and
`user_scenario` hands both over passively at the agent's direction: "When the agent hands that over to her
she does it there and then, without asking what it will cost her. In the same way, when the agent has the
closing figure and hands the closing over for her to do in person, she does it."

**Does the customer raise a prerequisite?** Not unprompted. The pre-buy is raised only on the agent's
initiative ("**If the agent tells her** the cooperative is holding a pre-buy she signed that never went onto
the account, she does remember …"), which is the passive form the persona contract allows. "She tells the
agent plainly that they may put whatever tidying the account needs through" is authorisation and names no
work. She names no additional item of work: "she will put a cheque in the post for it this week" is a future
act of her own and not an instruction to the agent. **O9 (observation):** "If the agent only quotes her a
figure and never hands anything over, she waits, and asks whether there is something she is meant to do" is
a nudge toward the hand-over; it names nothing and moves the agent past no gold action, so it is an
observation rather than a red light.

**Does the persona close where the gold path closes?** Yes — she reads the closing figure back, thanks the
agent and rings off on the closing write.

**SOURCE-CHAIN RED (C1) — the root's own prerequisite is not unmet at the opening.**
- symptom: the root's prerequisite sentence is satisfied at frozen_time, so a reader who walks down from the
  root never reaches any of the three prerequisite problems.
- root cause: the condition quantifies over bookings on the account ("for **every booking** whose gallons
  stand undrawn"), and the opening world has none; the tree's depth comes entirely from a booking the agent
  itself creates deeper in the same tree.
- evidence: `initial_state.energy_accounts["9762da2a-8ac5-4e50-9f1f-0df6113eb940"].contract_gallons = 0`,
  `.contract_price_per_gallon = 0.0`, `.current_gallons_owed = 0`; `initial_state.energy_deliveries` holds
  eighteen rows and none has `event_type: energy_contract_gallons_booked`. The declared `condition`
  ("Every booking on the account whose gallons stand undrawn carries an entry for the money applied against
  it when those gallons are released") is therefore vacuously true.
- demonstrated consequence: a solver who reads `energy_ext_closure_settlement`'s rule and the world, finds
  its only prerequisite satisfied, and computes the closing balance directly, gets a fully defensible
  **1745.71** (`amount_standing_d` 1806.80 — which is exactly the `account_balance` the account carries —
  plus a closing charge of 28.91 less a closing allowance of 90.00) instead of 3307.31. Removing this edge
  leaves the root with **no** prerequisite problem at all, so the tree collapses from three prerequisite
  problems to none.
- note in fairness: the chain is still *discoverable* by a different route — `energy_ext_prebuy_booking_
  credit`'s standing obligation ("A signed pre-buy request registered with the energy desk is put to the
  member's credit as booked gallons") together with the seeded `energy_orders` row, and base
  `energy_lifecycle_progression`'s "where contracted gallons stand undrawn they are dealt with under the
  programme's unused gallons treatment before the account can close". Neither is a prerequisite sentence of
  the root's own rule, and the second is a base sentence (see `_difficulty.md` O4).
- affected artifact: `energy.extended.yaml` → `energy_ext_closure_settlement` (`rule` last sentence of
  paragraph 1, `prerequisite[0].condition`); `tasks/energy_delivery_desk/tasks/1.json` → `initial_state`
  (`energy_accounts`, `energy_deliveries`).

### factor_weight

Recomputed on this task's own world at the 3.0900 reading of the booking price; gold figures are this
auditor's own, not any masked field.

**Computation A — `booked_gallons` (energy_ext_prebuy_booking_credit), gold 5200.**
Baseline alone: **5742.0** — definite and different from gold.

| factor | effect | honest? | tier taken | records putting the customer there | baseline from `baseline.rule` | value under it | weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| prior_use_window | method | yes — the window length changes | 2 | 6 stops in 12 months; `keep_full_enrolled: false` | "counted over the twelve months ending on the handling date" → 12 ✔ | 5600 | **bears** |
| prior_use_measure | method | yes — a grossing-up rule vs a halving vs raw | 1 | window 6 < 12; 6 stops | "the gallons taken on the account over that window as they stand" → `prior_use_raw` ✔ | 2600 | **bears** |
| input_ceiling_share | parameter | yes — a percentage | 1 | agronomy invoices 75 920.75 ≥ 60 000 **and** `agronomy_accounts.lien_on_file: true` (cross-difficulty: **agronomy**, two distinct records) | "The programme's ceiling share applies." → 110.0 ✔ | 4800 | **bears** |
| seasonal_use_allowance | parameter | yes — a gallons allowance | 1 | 2 420 gallons in three months ≥ 1 500; `tank_size_gallons` 2 000 ≥ 1 500 | "The seasonal allowance is nothing." → 0 ✔ | 5100 | **bears** |
| request_standing_share | parameter | yes — a share | 1 | `requested_date` 2025-11-20 (11 months); 6 stops | "The share the request's standing allows is the whole of it." → 1.0 ✔ | 5800 | **bears** |
| lot_rounding_rule | method | yes — a rounding rule | 1 | 7 000 ≥ 2 500; will-call tickets `ET-6712318`, `ET-6712611` inside three months | "The lot rule leaves the gallons unrounded." → `allowed_gallons` ✔ | 5230.08 | **bears** |

Counts: 6 factors, 3 `parameter`, 3 `method`. Multi-source: `input_ceiling_share` (invoice sum **and**
`lien_on_file`), `prior_use_window`, `seasonal_use_allowance`, `request_standing_share`,
`lot_rounding_rule`. Cross-difficulty: `input_ceiling_share` reads `agronomy_invoices.amount` and
`agronomy_accounts.lien_on_file`; both are seeded and consistent with the agronomy charter (an active
Seasonal Terms Crop Input Account with a perfected security interest).
**Stamp check:** clean. **Near-miss:** the 2026-05-05 delivery (1 100 gallons) sits at exactly six months
and is excluded from the short window, and the `agronomy_payment_posted` row of −34 670.00 would be summed

## findings

**1 — SOURCE-TASK RED (T1, confirmed and sharpened by the reveal): the booking price is not entailed by the
policy, and GT's stated basis for it is contradicted by the records.**
- symptom: `evaluation_criteria` step 8 scores `price_per_gallon = 2.9800`, and every later scored figure
  moves with it, while no rule in force fixes that figure.
- root cause: `energy_ext_prebuy_booking_credit` `computes: booked_gallons` only; its rule never mentions a
  price. Base `energy_contract_gallons_program` says only that "the money is taken at the booking rather
  than at delivery". Base `energy_pricing` anchors the posted price on "the day the fuel was pumped and not
  the day the invoice was cut" — a delivery anchor, not a request anchor — and no rack figure exists in any
  table or finder. `energy_orders.b3d73765-…` carries no price, and the persona supplies none.
- evidence: `evaluation_criteria[8].argument_uniqueness_tracing.price_per_gallon` reads: "the pre-buy rule
  fixes what booked gallons draw at through the programme's price basis … and **the only posting of record
  on the day the signed request was registered is the stop of 2025-10-15**, billed at 2.9800". Recomputed
  against the world: the signed request is dated **2025-11-20**
  (`initial_state.energy_orders.b3d73765-8138-4051-8ac2-f0112c2602d0.requested_date`) and **no**
  `energy_deliveries` row carries that date; the stop of 2025-10-15 is thirty-six days earlier. The
  sentence asserts a fact about the world that the world does not carry. Nor is 2.9800 a rack: it is the
  price *billed* on that ticket (`e555f3e9-….price_per_gallon = 2.98`), i.e. rack **plus** margin already.
- demonstrated consequence: the charter's own recurring phrase — "the price billed on the most recent stop
  the member called in", used verbatim in `energy_ext_contract_price_of_record` and in
  `energy_ext_undrawn_gallons_disposition` — gives **3.0900** and, running the same chain,
  price of record 3.0900, undrawn settlement 14506.40 and a closing balance of **3307.31** against GT's
  **2782.11**. Two further defensible readings (3.1400, 3.1200) give **3567.31** and **3463.31**. Four
  defensible answers for the scored `closing_balance_usd`.
- affected artifact: `energy.extended.yaml` → `energy_ext_prebuy_booking_credit` (`rule`, `computes`) and
  the base `energy_pricing` / `energy_contract_gallons_program` rules that leave the booking price unfixed;
  `task_tools.py` → `lodge_contract_gallon_booking_8fcb503b` (`price_per_gallon`, and
  `amount = booked_gallons × price_per_gallon`, which `energy_ext_closure_settlement.compute.commitment_d`
  consumes); `tasks/energy_delivery_desk/tasks/1.json` → `evaluation_criteria[8]`,
  `computations[1..3].expected`.
- relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**2 — SOURCE-CHAIN RED (C1, confirmed by GT's own rationale): the root's prerequisite is not unmet at the
opening; it is vacuously satisfied.**
- symptom: at frozen_time the root's prerequisite sentence is true, so a reader who walks down from the root
  never reaches any prerequisite problem.
- root cause: the edge's `condition` is universally quantified over bookings on the account
  ("**Every** booking on the account whose gallons stand undrawn carries an entry …") and the opening world
  carries no booking at all.
- evidence: `initial_state.energy_accounts["9762da2a-…"].contract_gallons = 0`,
  `.contract_price_per_gallon = 0.0`, `.current_gallons_owed = 0`; no `energy_deliveries` row has
  `event_type: energy_contract_gallons_booked`. GT states the vacuity in its own words and presents it as
  the edge being unmet: `prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false` — "The account
  carries no entry for money applied against any booking: the ledger holds seven stops, eight fee lines and
  three bank transfers and nothing else, and the account shows no gallons owed out of a pre-buy at all" —
  and `design_rationale`, PROBLEM-TREE CARD — "Unmet at frozen_time: **the account carries no booking at
  all, so it carries no release entry either.**" Under the condition as written, no bookings makes the
  condition true, not false. (Contrast the other two edges, whose `why_false` genuinely points at a false
  state: `contract_price_per_gallon = 0.0`, and a signed request standing unworked.)
- demonstrated consequence: an agent who reads `energy_ext_closure_settlement`'s rule, finds its only
  prerequisite satisfied and computes the closing balance on the opening world reaches a fully defensible
  **1745.71** (`amount_standing_d` 1806.80 — exactly the `account_balance` the seed carries — plus a closing
  charge of 28.91 less a closing allowance of 90.00) instead of 2782.11. Removing this edge leaves the root
  with **no** prerequisite problem, collapsing a tree of three prerequisite problems to none and taking the
  other two edges with it.
- affected artifact: `energy.extended.yaml` → `energy_ext_closure_settlement` (`rule` ¶1 last sentence,
  `prerequisite[0].condition`); `tasks/energy_delivery_desk/tasks/1.json` → `initial_state.energy_accounts`
  / `.energy_deliveries`, `prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time`,
  `design_rationale` PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
- relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**3 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (charter-global F5, demonstrated here, and GT asserts the base gate satisfied).**
- symptom: base forbids a member-initiated closure while anything is owed; the scored write closes the
  account carrying 2782.11, and the policy declares no override.
- root cause: `energy_ext_closure_settlement.overwrite: []` against base
  `energy_lifecycle_progression`'s "A member closes an account of their own accord with **nothing owing** …"
  and `params.closure_requires: [zero_balance, …]`.
- evidence: `_difficulty.md` § findings F5 for the two quotations. Recomputed on the world at step 14: the
  account owes `amount_standing_d` **2843.20** at the moment of the close and is closed carrying
  **2782.11**. `solvability_contract.gold_actions[step 14].base_preconditions[0]` quotes that very base
  sentence and records `"satisfied": true` — an assertion about the world contradicted by the
  recomputation. `user_scenario` puts the payment after the call ("she will put a cheque in the post for it
  this week"), so no payment write can precede the close.
- demonstrated consequence: two defensible answers, differing in the **terminal state**, not merely in a
  number — under the inherited base sentence the only correct act is to quote the figure and leave the
  account `active` until it is paid; under the extended policy the account moves to `closed` now with
  2782.11 written onto it.
- affected artifact: `energy.extended.yaml` → `energy_ext_closure_settlement` (`overwrite`, `rule`);
  `task_tools.py` → `close_energy_account_7515982f`; `tasks/energy_delivery_desk/tasks/1.json` →
  `evaluation_criteria[14]`, `solvability_contract.gold_actions[step 14].base_preconditions[0]`.
- relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**4 — SOURCE-POLICY RED (charter-global F4, demonstrated here).**
- symptom: the per-gallon cancellation charge on the released booking has two values.
- root cause: undeclared override of base `energy_contract_gallons_program`'s "pays the programme's
  cancellation charge per gallon cancelled" by the `cancellation_charge_relief` ladder.
- evidence: `_difficulty.md` § findings F4 (both sentences quoted, with
  `contract_cancellation_fee_per_gallon_usd: 0.1000`).
- demonstrated consequence: base → cancellation charge 0.1000, undrawn settlement **14272.40**, closing
  balance **2969.31**; extended → 0.0600, **14459.60**, **2782.11**. GT's own
  `computations[2].factor_sensitivity[2].baseline_result` is 14272.4, i.e. it records the base reading's
  figure as the factor's baseline while not declaring the override.
- affected artifact: `energy.extended.yaml` → `energy_ext_undrawn_gallons_disposition` (`overwrite`,
  `rule` ¶4, `compute.cancellation_rate`); scored solution: `computations[2].expected` and
  `computations[3].expected`, `evaluation_criteria` steps 12 and 14.
- relation to previous revisions: first revision.

**5 — observation (T2 and T3, withdrawn as red lights).** Both were frozen above on the 3.0900 booking
price and both were explicitly conditioned there on a booking price at or above 3.0200. On GT's 2.9800 the
truing rule takes its *second* tier (adjusted 3.0500 ≤ posted 3.0900 → the mean, 3.0700), so the clamp does
not bite, the three loadings are not swallowed, and `settlement_price_basis` separates min(3.07, 3.09) from
mean(3.07, 3.09). They are recorded here because the ladder shape that produces them is real and is only a
few cents away: any booking price at or above 3.0200 puts this task's computation B on a baseline equal to
gold with three decorative factors, and its computation C on a decorative `settlement_price_basis`. No
consequence is demonstrable on the world as seeded, so this is an observation, not a red light. Affected
artifact: `energy_ext_contract_price_of_record` (`factors[market_truing_rule]`, `baseline`),
`energy_ext_undrawn_gallons_disposition` (`factors[settlement_price_basis]`).

**6 — observation (O9, per-task).** `user_scenario`: "If the agent only quotes her a figure and never hands
anything over, she waits, and asks whether there is something she is meant to do." This fires only after
the agent has quoted a figure, names nothing and moves the agent past no gold action.
GT's `prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint` reaches the same conclusion. No consequence demonstrable.
Affected artifact: `tasks/energy_delivery_desk/tasks/1.json` → `user_scenario` ¶4.

**7 — observations carried from the charter-global scan that touch this task without a demonstrable
consequence here:** O1 (`prior_use_measure` and `volume_price_adjustment` have a stated third tier narrower
than `compute`'s `else`; this world lands in neither region), O2 (`energy_ext_contract_price_of_record`'s
`baseline.params` names two catalogue keys its baseline rule does not read), O4 (base
`energy_lifecycle_progression` states the closure-waits-on-disposition order, while the extended rule also
carries its own prerequisite sentence), O5 (a Bulk Farm Fuel Delivery Account is sold pre-buy gallons and
protection although its `price_basis` never prices a gallon at the contracted price), O6
(`closing_month_count` tier 2 charges an extra month for inactivity; it does not fire here). See
`_difficulty.md`.

**Proof-field verification (Step 3).** Every world-asserting sentence of `design_rationale`,
`solvability_contract`, `prerequisite_closure`, `factor_trace` and `argument_uniqueness_tracing` was
recomputed on the world of the moment it names. All check out — the ledger counts ("seven stops, eight fee
lines and three bank transfers", 18 rows), the draw record (`factor_counts: [5, 6, 6, 4]` against the
declared 6 / 5 / 6 / 4), all three `edge_load_bearing` figures and all twenty-one `factor_sensitivity`
figures — **except three**, each already red-lighted above:
`evaluation_criteria[8].argument_uniqueness_tracing.price_per_gallon` ("the only posting of record on the
day the signed request was registered"), `prerequisite_closure.edges[0].unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false`
together with the matching `design_rationale` line, and
`solvability_contract.gold_actions[step 14].base_preconditions[0].satisfied`.
